source.coverage: monster parts (mundane), venoms, special components, special component lists

identification.rule: Adventurers can identify the value of a monster's parts with a Naturalism proficiency throw of 11+ or a Loremastery throw.
Required proficiencies for efficient harvesting vary by part type and are specified in the relevant subsection.

sale_and_xp.rule: Harvested monster parts may be sold at market value, subject to equipment availability in markets.
Recovering monster parts during adventures does not grant treasure XP.
Monster parts may instead be sold as trade goods using mercantile venture rules.
For mercantile ventures, treat the base market value of the monster parts as the cost of goods sold.
Mercantile sale of monster parts can grant XP under mercantile venture rules.

rules.rule: Common animal horns are worth 10gp per stone of weight.
Exotic horns are worth 40gp to 100gp per stone of encumbrance.
Only male mammals should have antlers.
Horns can be sold or used as raw materials by a weaponsmith.
Horns can be used as precious materials when enchanting magical weapons.
Horns must be captured intact or they are worthless.
Horns are intact if the monster was not damaged with an area-of-effect attack.
A character with an axe or other cutting tool can remove horns from a dead or helpless monster in 6 rounds per stone of encumbrance.
Before sale, horns must be cleansed, trimmed, and polished.
Preparing a horn requires Animal Husbandry or Trapping proficiency and 1 turn per stone of encumbrance.
Baby, child, and adolescent monsters never have antlers, horns, or tusks.
Natural weapons harvested as trophies have encumbrance of 1 stone per 10gp of value.
If a monster has one or more claw or talon attacks, each claw or talon is worth gp equal to the maximum damage of that claw or talon attack.
If a monster has a bite attack, each fang is worth sp equal to the average damage of the bite.
If the monster can swallow man-sized creatures, its fangs are worth 10x the normal fang value, typically changing sp to gp.
For game purposes, a monster's fangs are its two largest and sharpest teeth or mandibles.
Very impressive teeth that function as tusks are handled under antlers_horns_and_tusks instead.
If a monster has a sting attack, its stinger is worth sp equal to the maximum damage of the sting.
If the sting delivers poison, stinger value is multiplied by 10.
For non-adult monsters, calculate natural weapon value using age-adjusted damage.
For monsters with STR 13 or more, include the damage bonus from high STR when calculating natural weapon value.
Large colorful feathers are typically worth 1gp to 6gp each and have encumbrance of 1 stone per 25 feathers.
Particularly impressive feathers can be larger and more valuable.
Giant roc feathers can be up to 20' long and worth 120gp each.
Feathers can be sold or used as raw materials by a fletcher.
Feathers can be used as precious materials when enchanting magical arrows or cloaks.
Feathers must be captured intact to maintain value.
Feathers are intact if the monster was not damaged with an area-of-effect attack.
Damaged feathers are worthless.
Plucking feathers takes 1 turn per stone of feathers.
Only notable feathers have market value: the 10 primary and 14 secondary flight feathers of each wing, plus the 12 tail flight feathers, for 60 total on a standard feathered creature.
Crossbreeds have fewer marketable feathers depending on body form.
Some marketable feathers may be missing due to age, weather, illness, or battle.
Baby, child, and adolescent monsters have feathers worth 25%, 50%, and 75% of adult value.
Adventurers may skin, flesh, and butcher slain monsters to harvest pelts and meat.
Time, amount yielded, and value are based on monster weight.
Proper preparation requires Animal Husbandry, Labor (butchery), Labor (farming), or Trapping.
Without one of the required proficiencies, each process takes double time and yields half amount.
Characters may collaborate in butchering by dividing monster weight among themselves.
All participating characters must have the appropriate craftsman's tools, even if unproficient.
Laborers can be hired at 1sp per 8 hours to skin, flesh, and butcher kills.
Labor cost equals 0.000625gp × monster weight in lbs.
Net profit after hired labor equals 0.01gp × monster weight in lbs.
Pelts can be made into rugs, capes, coats, and trophies.
Sewing or stuffing is a construction project with labor cost equal to final value minus value of pelts used.
Fur pelts of rare, durable, warm, or striking fur are worth 5gp per stone or more, up to 100gp per stone.

Intact fur pelts require that the monster was slain with one attack, or entirely with blunt weapons, or by cold, death magic, electricity, or poison while losing less than half its hit points to other attacks.
Damaged fur pelts are worth 1gp per stone.
Armored hides can be sold or used as raw materials by an armorer.
Armored hides can be used as precious materials when enchanting magical armor and shields.
Intact armored hides require that the monster was slain with one attack, or by cold, death magic, electricity, or poison while losing half its hit points or less to other attacks.
Damaged armored hides are worth 1gp per stone.
All pelts and armored hides must be skinned and fleshed before sale.
Baby, child, and adolescent monsters have pelts and meat worth 25%, 50%, and 75% of adult value.
If STR, CON, or CHA are 13-15, add 25% of pelt value for each such ability.
If STR, CON, or CHA are 16-17, add 100% of pelt value for each such ability.
If STR, CON, or CHA are 18, add 400% of pelt value for each such ability.
Bonuses from ability scores stack.
If STR, CON, or CHA are 3, reduce pelt value by 75% for each such ability.
If STR, CON, or CHA are 4-5, reduce pelt value by 50% for each such ability.
If STR, CON, or CHA are 6-8, reduce pelt value by 25% for each such ability.
Penalties from ability scores stack.
If stacked penalties reduce pelt value to 0 or less, the pelt is worthless.
Decimal stone weights are converted to items for encumbrance by rounding to the nearest 1/6.
Characters with Naturalism can identify venomous monsters and distinguish their poisons with a proficiency throw of 11+.
Extracting venom from a slain monster requires 1 day and a successful Animal Husbandry proficiency throw of 11+.
If the extraction throw is an unmodified 1, the extractor is scratched by fang or stinger and must immediately save versus Poison as if hit by the monster.
Each venomous monster yields 1 dose of venom.
One dose treats 20 missiles or 1 melee weapon.
Weapon-applied venoms are less effective than the monster's native delivery method.
Baby and child monsters do not have enough venom to extract.
Adolescent monsters have a full dose of venom.

condition.rule: Sickened characters move at ½ speed and cannot fight or perform other actions.

definition.rule: When a monster dies, a residue of its soul may linger in certain organs or bodily fluids.
These parts are special components usable in magic item creation and ritual spell casting.

rules.rule: Alchemy, Collegiate Wizardry, Magical Engineering, or Naturalism can identify the type of body part that is usually a special component for a species.
The base proficiency throw is 14+.
Reduce the target by 4 for each additional proficiency rank possessed in any of the relevant proficiencies, to a minimum target of 2+.
Failure means the adventurer does not know the typical special component for that species.
Loremastery may be used instead at its normal unmodified target value.
Roll 1d20 for unusual residue placement; on a natural 20, the monster has unusual special component(s) of the Judge's choice.
A spellcaster able to detect magic can determine the exact special component(s) of a particular slain monster.
Such spellcasters can also inspect harvested parts to determine whether they truly are special components.
This inspection takes 1 turn and requires a magic research throw.
On a failed magic research throw, the spellcaster gleans no information.
The spellcaster may retry every turn for as long as detect magic remains available.

intactness_rules.rule: Special components can only be harvested if captured intact.

optional_rule.name: permanent_wounds_and_harvesting
optional_rule.rule: When a monster is slain, roll on the Mortal Wounds table to see whether special components remain intact.
Select the Timing modifier based on when harvesting occurs.
Apply the +2 treatment modifier if the harvester has the prerequisite proficiency.
If the permanent wound damages or destroys the component, it cannot be harvested.
An instant kill result, defined as 0 or less on the modified d20, destroys all special components.

rules.rule: Appendages, external organs, and remnants can be harvested by any adventurer.
Harvesting appendages, external organs, and remnants takes 6 rounds per stone of encumbrance.
Bones, coverings, internal organs, and more exotic components require the listed prerequisite proficiencies.
Harvesters using prerequisite proficiencies must also have the appropriate craftsman's tools for the proficiency used.
Harvesting proficiency-gated components takes 1 turn per 100gp value of the component, minimum 1 turn.
Improperly stored special components have a cumulative 5% chance per day of losing all value.
Proper storage requires metamphora.
Metamphora cost 5gp and weigh 1 stone for every 60gp of value they can store.
With rare exceptions, a monster's total special component value equals its XP value.
Special component encumbrance is assumed to equal required metamphora encumbrance: 1 stone per 60gp value.
Bracketed restrictions in the table limit some associated spell effects to subsets of an entry.
Each monster type has default associated spell effects.
Every special component from a monster can be used for magical research relating to the default effects for that monster type.
Lawful monsters with innate divine magic are great-souled creatures.
Great-souled creatures have special components worth 10 times XP value.
Most ordinary animals cannot be harvested for special components.
Ordinary animals become harvestable only if they are dire, giant, prehistoric, or have total ability modifiers of +3 or more.
Creatures summoned temporarily by spells or scrolls can never be harvested for special components.
Creatures summoned by charged or permanent magic items can be harvested only up to maximum cumulative component value equal to the item's gp value.
Creatures permanently bound to this sphere, or slain in their own sphere, can be fully harvested.
If a monster part has both mundane and special-component value, and special-component value is only a fraction of mundane value, only that fraction of the part is consumed as a component.
If special-component value is less than mundane value, the remainder may be sold for mundane value minus special-component value.
If special-component value is equal to or greater than mundane value, the whole part is required as the component.
Baby, child, and adolescent monsters normally cannot be harvested for special components, except at Judge discretion.
The published lists are suggestive rather than exhaustive.
Each creature should have at least one special component.
Add one special component if the monster can carry a man-sized rider in flight.
Add one special component if the monster has at least 4 HD and three or more attacks per round.
Add one special component for each asterisk indicating special ability.
Creatures of purely artificial, elemental, incorporeal, or ooze substance should always have just one special component.
Associated effects may be selected by correspondence to the monster's abilities.
Associated effects may be selected by similarity to the monster's abilities or behavior.
Associated effects may be selected by polarity, using opposite behaviors or abilities.
Associated effects may be selected by contagion, using control, contact, or summoning effects related to the creature's type.
Associate winged flight only if wings are unnatural additions to the body form.
Associate flight only if the creature can carry a man-sized rider.
Associate infravision only if sight range is exceptional at 90'+.
Associate water breathing only if it is unnatural to the creature's body form.
Associate similar but inexact effects only if creature HD exceeds the spell level of the effect.
Total associated spell effects per monster should be capped at the greater of Hit Dice or number of special components.
Number of special components may be adjusted up or down by one or two to fit desired associated effects.
Total divine power possessed by a creature equals 10 times its XP value.
On death, about 90% transmigrates quickly and about 10% remains as residual special-component value.
On sacrifice, 80% passes to the worshipped entity, 10% is retained by the sacrificer, and 10% remains residual in blood and organs.
XP value = special component value = sacrifice value.
A living creature bleeds off divine power each day equal to 6% of its XP value.
When a cleric leads congregants in worship, the cleric collects about 10% of that bled-off divine power and the god receives the rest.
Dead creatures continue losing residual divine power over time unless their parts are properly stored.

confidence_notes.note: The Boar, Giant tusk value roll in the antlers_horns_and_tusks table appears OCR-corrupted as "1". I preserved the source reading, but the average suggests a lost die expression.
Several multi-component rows were split by OCR and reconstructed as separate rows: Thrassian, Faerie, Sprite, Nymph, Dryad, Nymph, Naiad, and Zombie.
Hell Hound, Greater appears split across lines; I reconstructed the teeth effects as ending with wall of fire and the tongue effects as detect invisible plus sphere of visibility.
Roc (any) encumbrance/value triples appear to be compressed small/large/giant values. I preserved the source numbers exactly.
Snake, Sea Snake includes OCR errors reading "snack charm" and singular "sticks to snake". I normalized this to snake charm and sticks to snakes.
A few capitalization and spelling forms appear OCR-inconsistent, such as Faravahar/Farahavar and Infravision/infravision. I used the form nearest the relevant table entry when possible.
